title: Native Vulkan quantised dot-product parity on REAL GGUF weights
scope: Closes the gap declared in RAWRXD_DEEP2_GPU_QUANT_DOT_001: 'Parity against real GGUF weights. The weights used here are synthetic'. This run loads REAL Q4_K and Q6_K tensor bytes from real GGUF files and compares the GPU kernel against a ggml-dequantised reference.

harness.gguf_reader: self-contained, memory-mapped; GGUF BOOL is 1 byte per the spec
harness.activation_source: row 0 of token_embd.weight dequantised by ggml, then quantised with the Q8_K rule d = amax/127
harness.note_on_activation_quantiser: The shader consumes one scale per 256 values (Q8_K style). ggml's Q8_0 uses one fp16 scale per 32 values. The harness therefore quantises with the Q8_K rule and reports the resulting difference vs ggml Q8_0 explicitly rather than silently reinterpreting per-32-scaled Q8_0 bytes.

references.A: ggml dequantises the real packed weights to F32 (type_traits::to_float) and dots with the same dequantised Q8 activation values the GPU saw. Shares no code with the shader.
references.B: Independent CPU implementation decoding the same block layouts with integer lanes (the RAWRXD_DEEP2_GPU_QUANT_DOT_001 reference). Cross-checks the shader against a third implementation.

models.kind: Nemotron-class decoder; same file used by deep2_token_profiler

q8_quantiser_cross_check.description: Our per-256 Q8_K-rule quantisation vs ggml's per-32 fp16 Q8_0, compared on dequantised values.
q8_quantiser_cross_check.explanation: Expected, not a defect: one scale per 256 values is coarser than one fp16 scale per 32. The harness fails hard above 0.10 relative L2.

what_this_establishes: The native Vulkan Q4_K and Q6_K kernels reproduce the reference on REAL quantised weights taken byte-for-byte from real GGUF files, not synthetic patterns.
Parity holds on both MoE expert tensors (Q4_K ffn_gate_exps, Q6_K ffn_down_exps) and a decoder output projection (Q6_K, dim 8192).
The GPU agrees with two independent references, so the agreement is not an artifact of a shared implementation.
what_this_does_not_establish: End-to-end Deep2 GPU inference. No executor calls ExecuteQuantDot yet.
Any performance or TPS claim. One invocation per row with host upload and readback is not a tuned matvec; this is a correctness run only.
MoE routing or expert-selection behaviour. Only the expert weight tensors were exercised.
GPU attention, RMSNorm, softmax, V aggregation, or KV-cache operations.
Numerical parity of a full transformer layer.
next: Wire ExecuteQuantDot into one ModelGenieExecutor projection and prove intermediate tensor parity end-to-end.
Extend to a multi-row dispatch (one invocation per tile, not per row) before any TPS measurement.
Implement the remaining primitives (attention, RMSNorm, softmax, V aggregation) before certifying a GPU-resident layer.
Only then measure GPU TPS: the weight-bandwidth finding from deep2_token_profiler (97% of decode time in mul_mat) says memory traffic is what must be reduced.
